description: QG-1 adversarial SQL corpus for the tsql dialect. Every case must be rejected by aida.query_gateway.QueryExecutionGateway's single validation pipeline -- zero bypasses is the exit condition.

cases.sql: SELECT dbo.fn_rate(c.customer_id) AS rate FROM retail.customer AS c
cases.description: a dbo-qualified scalar function: user-defined, refused unless authorized by its qualified name

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id FROM retail.customer; DROP TABLE retail.customer;
cases.description: a second statement appended after a semicolon; DDL smuggled behind a syntactically valid first statement

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id FROM retail.customer; SELECT 1;
cases.description: batching is refused even when the second statement is itself harmless -- the rule is about ungovernable batches, not about what the batch contains

cases.sql: DELETE FROM retail.customer WHERE customer_id = 1
cases.description: a mutation submitted directly to a read-only gateway

cases.sql: DROP TABLE retail.customer
cases.description: DDL submitted where only a read-only query is accepted

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id INTO evil_table FROM retail.customer
cases.description: SELECT ... INTO writes a new table at the source under cover of a SELECT

cases.sql: SELECT * FROM retail.customer
cases.description: an unbounded projection that cannot be classification-checked or masked

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id FROM retail.customer, retail.account
cases.description: an implicit cross join via comma syntax -- no ON, no USING

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id FROM retail.customer c JOIN retail.account a ON true
cases.description: a join condition with the shape of an ON clause but no substance -- the same cartesian product as a cross join, disguised past a naive 'has an ON clause' check

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id FROM retail.customer c JOIN retail.account a ON 1=1
cases.description: the classic tautological join predicate

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id FROM retail.customer WITH (UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK)
cases.description: T-SQL spells a locking read as a table hint rather than FOR UPDATE -- WITH (UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK) takes and holds update locks against a shared source through a stateless gateway

cases.sql: WITH leak AS (SELECT ssn FROM fin.employee) SELECT ssn FROM leak
cases.description: an unauthorized table reached only inside a CTE definition, then surfaced through the CTE's own alias

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id, (SELECT ssn FROM fin.employee LIMIT 1) AS leaked FROM retail.customer
cases.description: an unauthorized table reached through a scalar subquery in the projection list rather than the top-level FROM

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id FROM retail.customer/**/UNION/**/SELECT ssn FROM fin.employee
cases.description: block comments used to break up keywords past a naive string-matching filter; parsed correctly here because the guard works on the AST, not the source text, so the comment changes nothing structurally

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id FROM retail.customer WHERE note = 'x''; DROP TABLE retail.customer; --' AND customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM retail.customer) UNION SELECT ssn FROM fin.employee
cases.description: a SQL-metacharacter-laden string literal (properly escaped, so it remains one opaque value) paired with a real UNION against an unauthorized table -- proves the literal's contents never parse as a second statement, and the union is still caught on its own merits

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id FROM retail.customer UNION SELECT ssn FROM fin.employee
cases.description: UNION used to append rows from a table outside the approved projection

cases.sql: SELECT xp_cmdshell('dir') AS out
cases.description: OS command execution called as a scalar function inside a SELECT, not via EXEC -- no table reference at all, so nothing for a catalog-only check to catch

cases.sql: SELECT col1 FROM OPENQUERY(LinkedServer, 'SELECT password FROM sys.users') AS r(col1)
cases.description: a linked-server rowset used as a FROM source -- the embedded SQL string is opaque to sqlglot and the source object is never an `exp.Table`, so it cannot be resolved against the metadata catalog at all

cases.sql: SELECT a FROM OPENROWSET('SQLNCLI', 'Server=x;Trusted_Connection=yes;', 'SELECT 1') AS r(a)
cases.description: ad hoc remote connection used as a table source, bypassing the datasource's own credential and catalog binding entirely

cases.sql: SELECT sp_executesql(N'SELECT 1') AS x
cases.description: dynamic SQL execution called as a function -- the argument string is never parsed or governed by this pipeline

cases.sql: EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options', 1
cases.description: server configuration change via EXEC, not a query at all

cases.sql: EXEC xp_cmdshell 'dir'
cases.description: OS command execution via the classic EXEC form
